contentBlocks.body: typeof and in narrow simple cases, but real data often arrives as unknown: a parsed JSON body, a message from another window, a value read from localStorage. A user-defined type guard is a function that checks a value at runtime and returns value is User. When it returns true, TypeScript narrows the argument to User in the calling code.

The compiler trusts your guard completely. If isUser returns true for something that is not really a User, the types lie. Check every field you rely on, and remember that typeof null is "object" and arrays are objects too.

Guards compose well with array methods: values.filter(isUser) has the type User[] because filter has an overload that accepts a type predicate. A plain boolean callback would leave you with unknown[].
